questions: Can the edge reversal operation be performed multiple times, and does each reversal toggle the direction of all edges (i.e., reversing again restores original directions)?
Is the edge reversal operation allowed at any vertex, or only at specific vertices (e.g., only at vertices with outgoing edges)?
Does moving along a directed edge require that the edge exists in the current orientation (after any reversals) at the moment of movement?
If an edge is reversed, does the reversal affect all edges globally and instantaneously, or only edges incident to the current vertex?
Is the goal to minimize total cost to reach vertex N, or is any sequence of operations acceptable as long as vertex N is reached?
Can the edge reversal operation be performed consecutively without moving in between, and if so, does each reversal incur cost X?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how do they behave under reversal?
Is the graph static aside from the reversals, or can edges be added/removed during operations?
